policy.purpose: Evidence ledger for the published canonical 100-pattern production set.
policy.primary_palette_rule: A fixed primary palette is an editorial recognition reference unless a source establishes color as identity-relevant. The palette itself is never presented as the only valid colorway.
policy.relationship_rule: similar and often_confused_with are visual-discovery relationships, not claims of shared historical origin unless explicitly sourced.
policy.qualification_rule: Use qualified when the term is fundamentally a technique, textile tradition, textile style, or material-inspired visual family that does not resolve to one uniquely fixed motif.

patterns.term_scope: two-color broken twill/check pattern
patterns.structure: Two-color broken twill/check producing jagged four-pointed forms.

color_guidance.reason: High-contrast recognition reference; the definition requires two colors, not specifically black and white.

sources.publisher: Museum of Fine Arts Boston / CAMEO

patterns.term_scope: checked cotton cloth / check appearance
patterns.structure: Woven colored squares/checks on a white ground; the surface appearance comes from crossing colored and white yarns.

color_guidance.reason: White plus a colored check is characteristic; blue is only the fixed reference color.

patterns.term_scope: registered woven design / repeated sett
patterns.structure: Two or more alternating colored stripes repeat vertically and horizontally to form a chequered sett.

color_guidance.reason: Color sequence and stripe proportions are part of a specific tartan's sett; the chosen palette is not itself a registered tartan claim.

supports: role of color sequence and stripe proportions

color_guidance.reason: Muted or black/gray/white combinations are documented as common, but are not the sole valid palette.

patterns.term_scope: diamond-pattern family used especially in knitwear
patterns.structure: Repeating colored diamonds/lozenges; many common forms add crossing diagonal lines over the diamonds.

color_guidance.reason: Multiple colors are characteristic, but no single palette defines argyle.

patterns.term_scope: geometric V/zigzag motif family
patterns.structure: Repeated V-shaped or zigzag bands/units.

color_guidance.reason: Geometry, not color, defines the recognition target.

supports: historic textile-design use of a chevron base pattern

patterns.term_scope: regular repeated round-dot surface pattern
patterns.structure: Many small round spots repeated in a regular pattern.

color_guidance.reason: Round repeated dots define the pattern; color is variable.

supports: Japanese water-dot wording mapped to polka-dot pattern

patterns.term_scope: contemporary decorative/design-market descriptor
patterns.structure: A repeating lattice cell with rounded sides and pointed top/bottom or related quatrefoil-like variants.

color_guidance.reason: No evidence supports a defining historical palette for this market label.

patterns.qualification: The name is well established in contemporary interiors and pattern-market usage, but the reviewed sources do not establish one uniquely canonical historic Moroccan motif under this exact name. Detail copy must avoid claiming a single traditional provenance.

sources.publisher: Isthmus / University of Wisconsin design commentary

patterns.term_scope: ornamental vegetal pattern vocabulary
patterns.structure: Rhythmical scrolling vine and foliate forms, often with bifurcating vines and split leaves that imply continuing extension.

color_guidance.reason: The ornamental structure, not palette, defines the entry.

patterns.term_scope: boteh-derived ornamental motif family

patterns.term_scope: resist-dye textile technique and resulting visual family, not one fixed motif

color_guidance.reason: Ikat spans many regions, motifs and palettes; no single color set defines the technique.

patterns.qualification: The dictionary entry must explicitly say that ikat is fundamentally a dyeing/weaving technique and visual family, not a single geometric motif.

supports: technique creates diverse imagery rather than one motif

patterns.term_scope: flat-woven textile category and kilim-inspired visual family, not one fixed motif
patterns.structure: Flat-woven/tapestry-woven textile tradition with diverse regional designs; angular geometric bands, diamonds and stepped forms are common in kilim-inspired surface design but are not one universal canonical motif.

color_guidance.reason: Kilim traditions use diverse colors and designs; the fixed palette is only a recognition reference.

patterns.qualification: Production copy must distinguish kilim itself (a flat-woven textile category) from 'kilim pattern' as a modern visual-search label for designs inspired by those textiles.

patterns.term_scope: small even check family

ja: シェパードチェック柄

patterns.structure: Small, even checks formed by contrasting stripes, classically black and white.

color_guidance.reason: Black-and-white is explicitly documented as a classic construction, but the pattern family is not restricted to one palette.

patterns.term_scope: Madras textile/check style rather than one fixed grid specification

patterns.qualification: Madras is also a cloth/textile term and historical textile tradition, not a single immutable check geometry. Detail copy must not present one reference repeat as the only authentic Madras pattern.

タッタソールチェック

ja: ガンクラブチェック柄

patterns.structure: A small repeating check using multiple tones/colors, commonly understood as a shepherd-check or related base varied with additional colors/check layers.

glen-check base plus windowpane overcheck as practical distinction

patterns.structure: Very narrow, usually pale parallel stripes on a darker cloth, especially associated with tailoring.

color_guidance.reason: Pale narrow lines on a dark ground are well documented, but exact colors are variable.

patterns.term_scope: balanced alternating colored-and-white stripe convention

ja: ベンガルストライプ柄

patterns.structure: Evenly spaced stripes of alternating color and white, typically broader than fine pin/pencil stripes.

color_guidance.reason: Alternating white and color is structural; blue is only a familiar recognition reference.

patterns.term_scope: broad Japanese lattice/check family
patterns.structure: Vertical and horizontal stripes/lines intersect to form a lattice of rectangular or square cells; many named subtypes vary line weight, count, and spacing.

color_guidance.reason: Line intersection defines the family; color is not intrinsic.

patterns.qualification: Koushi/格子 is a broad Japanese pattern family with many variants, not one unique repeat. Detail copy must distinguish this line-based lattice family from Ichimatsu's alternating filled squares.

verified_names.ja: オーニングストライプ

ja: オーニングストライプ柄

patterns.structure: Bold, broad, regularly repeated stripes recalling traditional shop or outdoor awnings.

color_guidance.reason: Large stripe scale is defining; exact color is variable.

patterns.term_scope: stripe style associated with English/British regimental ties rather than one fixed repeat

verified_names.ja: レジメンタルストライプ

patterns.structure: A repeated stripe arrangement recognizable through its relationship to striped British regimental neckwear; exact widths, colors, and direction vary.

patterns.qualification: Regimental Stripe is a style/family label tied to regimental neckwear conventions, not one universal color sequence, stripe width, or direction. The dictionary must avoid assigning one generic stripe as an authentic regiment-specific design.

patterns.term_scope: French maritime clothing/style convention derived from striped naval knitwear
patterns.structure: Horizontal contrasting stripes, classically blue/navy and white, strongly associated with the French maritime/Breton top tradition.

color_guidance.reason: Blue-and-white horizontal striping is central to the historic naval reference, while modern Breton-style garments vary spacing and colors.

patterns.qualification: The historic French naval garment had specific uniform dimensions, but modern 'Breton stripe' is a broader fashion convention. Detail copy must distinguish the historical marinière specification from contemporary Breton-style stripes.

patterns.term_scope: dotted Swiss textile/fabric category, not generic printed polka dots
patterns.structure: Fine, sheer, crisp fabric carrying small dots on its surface; the dots may be woven, embroidered, flocked, or otherwise applied depending on the textile.

color_guidance.reason: Texture and dotted surface treatment matter more than color; white-on-white is a neutral recognition reference.

patterns.qualification: Swiss Dot/Dotted Swiss fundamentally names a dotted fabric/textile treatment. The dictionary must not collapse it into ordinary flat printed polka dots, and the reference image should convey textile surface/relief.

patterns.term_scope: herringbone weave/arrangement and its broken-V visual family
patterns.structure: Adjacent rows of short slanting strokes reverse direction to form repeated broken V shapes or zigzag columns.

color_guidance.reason: Direction reversal and broken-V structure define recognition; color is variable.

patterns.qualification: Herringbone can denote a textile weave, a broader visual arrangement, embroidery, brickwork, and other constructions. In Pattern Dictionary it is represented as the visual family while clearly distinguishing the common woven form from a simple printed Chevron/Zigzag.

supports: herringbone as a weave variation on twill

patterns.term_scope: generic angular line/pattern family

color_guidance.reason: Angular path geometry, not color, defines the generic family.

patterns.term_scope: generic repeated diamond/rhombus geometric family
patterns.structure: Repeated diamond/rhombus shapes, typically four-sided forms with equal sides and acute/obtuse opposite angles rather than a required color or internal line system.

color_guidance.reason: The repeated rhombus geometry defines the family.

supports: historic textile use of a repeated/stepped diamond pattern

patterns.term_scope: diamond-block pattern convention associated with Harlequin costume

color_guidance.reason: Contrasting diamond blocks are characteristic; no single modern palette is universal.

patterns.term_scope: generic alternating dark/light square pattern

patterns.term_scope: named rectilinear meander motif
patterns.structure: A continuous rectilinear line turns at right angles to form a repeated meander, commonly used as a border or band.

color_guidance.reason: The right-angled meander geometry carries recognition; color is not intrinsic to the motif.

patterns.term_scope: named four-lobed motif
patterns.structure: A symmetrical four-lobed figure with four rounded leaves or lobes separated by cusps.

color_guidance.reason: Recognition depends on the four-lobed outline rather than a fixed palette.

patterns.term_scope: ogee double-curve form used as a repeating surface-design family

color_guidance.reason: The double-curve silhouette is the recognition cue; color is not definitional.

patterns.qualification: Ogee is fundamentally an S-shaped or double-curved profile used in architecture and design, not one universal textile motif. Pattern Dictionary treats repeated opposed or interlocking ogee curves as a qualified surface-design family.

patterns.term_scope: generic crossed-strip or crisscross pattern family

patterns.term_scope: generic honeycomb-derived cellular pattern

patterns.term_scope: generic repeated scalloped-arc pattern family

color_guidance.reason: The repeated rounded shell-like arcs carry recognition; palette is variable.

patterns.term_scope: weave structure and basket-like visual family

color_guidance.reason: Interlaced grouped structure is the key cue; natural basket colors are only illustrative.

patterns.qualification: Basketweave is a weave structure and visual effect, not one universal printed motif. The reference image may depict the interlaced basket-like appearance but must not imply one canonical thread count or construction.

patterns.term_scope: generic repeated six-sided polygon pattern

patterns.term_scope: generic trellis-derived repeat family

color_guidance.reason: The open framework/repeat structure is the cue; no one palette defines trellis patterns.

patterns.term_scope: Japanese diamond/rhombus motif family

color_guidance.reason: Rhombus geometry and Japanese motif context define recognition; indigo/white is illustrative only.

patterns.term_scope: named stylized lily/iris motif

sources.publisher: Getty Research Institute, Art & Architecture Thesaurus

patterns.term_scope: printed-textile/design tradition associated with pictorial figural scenes

color_guidance.reason: Single-color pictorial printing on a light ground is a strong recognition convention, but historical examples use multiple ink colors and subjects.

patterns.qualification: Toile de Jouy is a textile and printing/design tradition associated with Jouy-en-Josas and pictorial printed cottons, not one fixed repeat or exclusively pastoral scene. The reference image is a representative recognition example only.

patterns.term_scope: printed cotton/textile tradition commonly associated with floral patterning
patterns.structure: Printed or painted cotton commonly presents dense flowers, foliage, branches, and other decorative motifs across the surface; glazed finishes are historically common.

color_guidance.reason: Multicolor floral imagery is a strong recognition convention, but chintz is not defined by one palette or one repeat.

patterns.qualification: Chintz is historically a cotton textile/material and printing or painting tradition, not one fixed floral motif. Modern visual discovery often uses the word for dense floral prints, so Pattern Dictionary keeps that usage explicitly qualified.

patterns.term_scope: generic small-flower print pattern
patterns.structure: Many small flowers or similarly small motifs are scattered across the ground, typically at a fine scale and without a dominant large bloom.

color_guidance.reason: Small-scale scattered floral density matters more than a particular colorway.

verified_names.ja: ジャコビアン・フローラル

patterns.structure: Scrolling stems carry stylized flowers, leaves, fruit, and sometimes animals or tree-like compositions in a dense ornamental arrangement.

patterns.qualification: Jacobean Floral is a modern surface-design label derived from a broader historical Jacobean embroidery and crewelwork style, not one fixed motif. The reference repeat must represent characteristic scrolling botanical forms without claiming a universal Jacobean pattern.

patterns.term_scope: named dense field of many small flowers
patterns.structure: Numerous small flowering plants and blossoms densely fill the field so that the surface reads as a continuous flower-strewn ground.

color_guidance.reason: Dense multiplicity of small flowers is the core cue; historical palettes and media vary.

patterns.term_scope: broad plant-form surface-print family
patterns.structure: Leaves, stems, flowers, seedpods, or other recognizable or abstracted plant forms organize the surface, ranging from naturalistic illustration to stylized repeats.

color_guidance.reason: Plant-form subject matter defines the family; palette and level of naturalism vary widely.

patterns.qualification: Botanical Print is a broad modern discovery label for plant-based imagery rather than one historically fixed motif or repeat. Sources support botanical forms as textile-pattern subject matter and current botanical-print usage, so the reference image is representative rather than canonical.

patterns.term_scope: generic ivy-leaf botanical motif family
patterns.structure: Recognizable lobed ivy leaves repeat alone or along stems and vines, often layered or trailing across the surface.

color_guidance.reason: Green supports immediate ivy recognition, but leaf silhouette and vine organization are the real cues and other palettes are valid.

patterns.qualification: Ivy Pattern is a broad botanical motif family, not one standardized repeat. The museum source verifies an ivy textile pattern and layered-leaf treatment, but Pattern Dictionary must not present that one arrangement as the universal ivy pattern.

patterns.term_scope: same or sharkskin fine-dot komon visual produced within a fine-pattern dyeing tradition

color_guidance.reason: Minute dotted arc structure defines the visual; Edo/Tokyo komon is produced in many colors.

patterns.qualification: Same Komon is a named fine-dot pattern, but it is also embedded in the stencil-dyed komon technique and craft tradition. Pattern Dictionary therefore qualifies the entry so the dotted sharkskin visual is not confused with all Edo/Tokyo Some-Komon or with one fixed stencil density.

patterns.term_scope: named Japanese comma-shaped tomoe motif

patterns.term_scope: family of Japanese resist-dye techniques producing many different patterns

patterns.qualification: Shibori is a family of resist-dye techniques, not one pattern. Any reference image is necessarily representative of one shibori visual outcome and must not be presented as canonical for the entire tradition.

color_guidance.reason: Traditional palettes vary by region and practice; wax-resist construction is more fundamental than any color pair.

patterns.term_scope: South Asian tie-resist textile technique and tradition characterized by numerous tied points

color_guidance.reason: Bright contrasting colors are common recognition cues, but tying method and dotted resist structure define the craft more than palette.

patterns.qualification: Bandhani is a tie-resist technique and textile tradition capable of producing many named layouts, not one universal dotted repeat. Pattern Dictionary uses a characteristic dotted resist field as a representative visual only.

patterns.qualification: Ajrakh is a textile-printing tradition and process, not one fixed motif. Its recognizable geometric vocabulary and common dye family can guide discovery, but no single star, medallion, grid, or layout is canonical for all Ajrakh.

patterns.qualification: Kalamkari names a textile-making process and regional tradition spanning hand-painted and related printed works with many compositions. It is not one universal motif, so the reference image must be presented as representative rather than canonical.

patterns.term_scope: Central Asian embroidered textile tradition with many regional compositions rather than one fixed repeat
patterns.structure: Large embroidered rosettes, palmettes, flowers, stems and scrolling foliage are arranged across joined cotton or silk panels; composition varies by region and workshop.

patterns.qualification: Suzani is a Central Asian embroidered textile tradition, not one universal repeat. The reference image is a representative recognition aid.

patterns.term_scope: Ghanaian strip-woven textile tradition with many named arrangements rather than one fixed motif

patterns.qualification: Kente is a Ghanaian strip-woven textile tradition with many designs and meanings, not one canonical repeat.

patterns.term_scope: Malian bogolanfini mud-dyed textile tradition with varied symbolic pattern vocabularies
patterns.structure: High-contrast dark and light fields use repeated lines, dots, chevrons and symbolic geometric units produced in a mud-dye textile tradition; exact layouts vary.

color_guidance.reason: Dark mud-dyed marks against pale cloth are a strong recognition cue; exact motifs vary.

patterns.qualification: Bogolan/bogolanfini is a mud-dyed Malian textile tradition with many encoded or named pattern arrangements, not one fixed motif.

patterns.term_scope: Yoruba indigo resist-dyed textile tradition using multiple resist methods and named patterns

patterns.term_scope: Kuba textile tradition using raffia and varied geometric embroidery/applique rather than one fixed motif

patterns.qualification: Kuba cloth denotes a broad Central African raffia textile tradition with many techniques and patterns, not one universal repeat.

patterns.term_scope: Japanese running-stitch reinforcement and embroidery tradition with many geometric motifs
patterns.structure: Repeated running stitches form dotted white lines on cloth, often organized into grids, waves, diamonds, hemp-leaf-like geometry, or other named Japanese motifs.

color_guidance.reason: White running stitches on indigo are a strong traditional recognition cue, but sashiko exists in other colors.

patterns.qualification: Sashiko is a Japanese stitching and reinforcement tradition with many patterns, not one fixed motif.

patterns.term_scope: Bengal/Bangladesh layered-cloth running-stitch embroidery and quilting tradition with varied personal designs

patterns.qualification: Kantha is a Bengal/Bangladesh quilting and embroidery tradition with diverse individual compositions, not one fixed repeat.

patterns.term_scope: Otomí/Tenango embroidery tradition with varied densely filled animal and plant figures

color_guidance.reason: Multicolor filled silhouettes are a common recognition cue, while palettes vary.

patterns.qualification: Otomi/Tenango embroidery is a living textile tradition with diverse compositions, not one fixed repeat.

patterns.term_scope: Relief block-printing technique capable of many textile motifs rather than one fixed visual pattern
